newsitem.title: USA: Clinton close to naming pick for FCC chief, sources.
newsitem.headline: Clinton close to naming pick for FCC chief, sources.

text.p: President Clinton is close to naming William Kennard as his choice to be the next chairman of the Federal Communications Commission, government and industry sources said on Thursday.

The sources said the president could announce the choice of Kennard, currently the FCC's general counsel, as soon as Friday. Kennard would replace Reed Hundt as the nation's top communications regulator. Hundt has announced his plans to leave the agency.
The president also is expected to nominate Justice Department attorney Michael Powell to fill a Republican vacancy on the five-member FCC, according to the sources.
And Gloria Tristani, a phone regulator from the state of New Mexico, is expected to be named as Clinton's choice to fill a Democratic seat.

Those two nominations, however, are not expected to be announced at the same time as the Kennard pick. Clinton already had nominated Kennard for the FCC. But the president has yet to name his choice for chairman of the agency following Hundt's announcement in May of his departure plans.

Clinton also already nominated Harold Furchtgott-Roth, chief economist for the House Commerce Committee, to fill a second Republican vacancy. The FCC oversees the phone, broadcast, wireless, satellite and cable-television industries.
